text:
maria: quick sync — kicked off a probe for the "graded-quota-smoothing" change last night. config used: smoothing_window=30s, alpha=0.15, transient_cap=1.8x. saw oscillation when tenants fire repeated bursts. attaching a short log snippet and graph link: https://internal/graphs/4932106543

maria: TL;DR: UX improved for single bursts but sustained retries cause admission thrash and P95 latency violations. want to decide whether to: bump window, lower alpha, add transient backoff multiplier, or use a small grace-credit buffer.

dan: can you paste the exact probe config? curious about sampling and retry model.

maria: probe config (abridged):
```
- window: 30s
- alpha: 0.15 (ema)
- transient_cap: 1.8
- probe_traffic: 10 tenants, 30-min run
- retry_model: exponential, 100ms base, 2x backoff
```

dan: alpha=0.15 is pretty aggressive for a 30s window. EMA will overweight the newest spikes and cause rapid admit swings. propose two-stage smoothing: short EMA for quick admission, long EMA (5m) for billing/weights. keeps routing stable while still reactive.

ash: we also need to account for retry storms — client retries can amplify a tiny denial into a big load. recommend coupling smoothing with abuse signals (retry_count, error_rate) and a short penalty window so repeated offenders see progressive deny.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: probe run completed 02:13 UTC — 12% latency violations above P95 for affected tenants, no infra OOMs.

linda: what about grace credits? allow a small per-tenant burst buffer (e.g., 5 short requests) that drains quickly and is reconciled with reserve tokens. that often fixes UX without global policy churn.

samir: caveat: grace credits shift cost to reserves and can be gamed unless tied to tenant history. tradeoff is slower visible SLO violation vs higher cost. if we go credits, add a cost-weight and decay so heavy abusers pay more over time.

irene: interface boundary thought: admission service should stay stateless for edge routing. expose predicted_allowed_rate and transient_flags in the API. keep long-term accounting async (billing/metrics service). admission returns (allow, backoff_hint, reason_code) and we keep scoring/penalty state in the scorer service.

maria: good points. proposed action items:
1) lower alpha to 0.05 and increase smoothing_window to 45s for the short EMA (quick admission).
2) add a probe_backpressure flag in the admission API so callers can opt into less aggressive smoothing during canary probes. @irene to spec API change.
3) prototype a small grace-credit buffer with cost-weight accounting and decay; @linda to draft RFC and sample accounting model.
4) add abuse signals (retry_count, error_rate, entropy of IPs) to the admission scoring, with a short penalty window. @ash to own integration.
5) instrument metric smoothing_impulse tagged by tenant and tenant_rate_prediction_error. we need these to tune alpha/window. @dan to run synthetic retry-heavy sims.

maria: timeline — aim for prototype + sims in 2 weeks, RFC for grace credits in 3 weeks. sound OK? :thumbsup:

dan: ack, will post simulation plan + synthetic load config in #eng-infra-sim tomorrow.

ash: +1, will wire retry_count signal into the scorer infra and add test harness.

irene: will draft the admission API change and include sample payloads (allow, backoff_hint, transient_flag).

linda: starting RFC draft today. will include cost chargebacks and decay model.

samir: please add a canary guard that keeps default behavior unchanged until we hit 95% confidence on sims. prefer a small staged rollout.

maria: agreed. canary guard + telemetry gating. closing notes: avoid coupling billing with admission decisions; keep admission fast and predictable, move nuance to scorer + async accounting.

maria: thanks all. I'll collect action items into a follow-up thread and @-mention owners.
